changelog: First public release of fx-admin — modern, themed, optimized admin panel for QBCore, Qbox and ESX.

New Gang Management page: the full Job Management toolset - bulk and per-selection removal, transfer to another gang, grade reset, single and bulk CK with backup and restore, member list with online/offline filter, search and CSV export - now works on gangs too. Jobs and gangs are two separate pages under the Jobs & Gangs nav group.

Jobs and gangs share ONE code path instead of duplicated code. Every layer (framework, database, business logic, UI) takes a kind parameter that is either job or gang, so a later fix lands on both sides at once. Omitting it means job, so nothing that called these functions before had to change.

Gang operations write to players.gang through SetGang using the gang JSON schema (no payment/onduty fields). Counts, personnel queries and the reset/transfer UPDATEs all pick their column from the category, and the count cache is now per category - one shared cache would have let gang counts overwrite job counts.

Discord logs are category-aware. Gang operations can go to their own Config.GangLogsWebhook and fall back to JobLogsWebhook then LogsWebhook. Embed title, field names (Old Gang / New Gang) and footer follow the category, and CK records from this page are tagged gangck so CK History and the restore log label them correctly.

Recent Actions is filtered per category: the job page no longer shows gang operations and vice versa. Entries written before this release carry no category field and are treated as job, so existing history stays intact.

New config keys: Config.JobManagement.GangResetTarget (default "none") is the gang a removed member is moved to, and Config.GangLogsWebhook (empty = falls back to the job webhook). Config.JobManagement.HistoryLimit is shared between job and gang history - raise it if both sides are used heavily.
ESX has no gang concept, so the Gang Management page stays empty there and every gang operation is rejected with a nogang error instead of silently touching the player job.
Fixed: the jobmgmt.hard_grade_desc locale string was cut off mid-sentence in both tr and en, so the final grade-reset confirmation showed half a sentence.

Ambulance / death-system bridge: revive and full heal now go through whichever medical script the server runs, instead of only restoring health on the ped. Wasabi Advanced Ambulance is supported in both v1 and v2 (folder named wasabi_ambulance, wasabi_ambulance_v2 or wasabi_ambulancev2), alongside the existing qb-ambulancejob, Renewed-Ambulance and esx_ambulancejob.

Fixed: on servers running Wasabi, revive reported success and did nothing. The panel, the /revive keybind and the Discord /revive and /revive-all commands all restored health while Wasabi kept its own death state, so the player stayed down and was told they had been revived. Wasabi revives from the server through an export, not from the client, so the whole flow was moved server side.

Fixed: full heal left Wasabi players capped and still bleeding. Wasabi derives max health from limb damage and keeps injuries server side, so healing the ped alone could not clear them. Heal now clears injuries and limb health through the script, and no longer writes health from the client where Wasabi owns that value.
New config key: Config.Ambulance (default auto) pins the medical script - auto, wasabi, qb, renewed, esx or none.

Fixed: CK History could not find older records. The list only ever carried the newest 200 rows and the search box filtered those rows in the browser, so a CK outside that window read as 'not found' in the panel even though the backup was still in the database and still restorable. Search and the status tabs now run as SQL on the server, so every record is reachable regardless of the list window.

CK History search accepts Discord ID, Steam hex and license as well as name, citizenid, job and the admin who performed the CK. The backup table stores only citizenid and license, so a Discord ID or Steam hex is resolved through the identifier ledger first - the Discord lookup also scans online players, so an account never written to the ledger is still found.

Fixed: the counters above CK History showed the list length instead of the real totals, so Total CK Records sat pinned at the 200 ceiling and told the admin that was all of them. They are now counted across the whole table.

CK History selection survives a new search. The restore basket keeps the record itself, not just its id, so selecting one character and then searching for another no longer drops the first from the basket.

txAdmin ban sync now reads txAdmin's live playersDB.json on hosts that sandbox file access to the resource folder. Symlink playersDB.json to fx-admin/txdata_players.json and the panel reads the real file - no copy to refresh, no stale snapshot. Lua's file API follows the link even inside the sandbox, which is what makes this work where an absolute path is refused.

Fixed: a symlinked txdata_players.json made the import fail completely. FiveM's virtual file system ignores a Windows reparse point, so the only reader fx-admin used could not see the link, and the import reported the file as missing while the data sat right there. Reading now goes through Lua's file API first and falls back to the virtual file system, so both a symlink and a plain copy work.

New config key: Config.TxAutoSyncMinutes (default 120) re-imports txAdmin bans on a timer. Bans issued while fx-admin is running already arrive instantly through txAdmin's events; the timer closes the gap for bans issued while fx-admin was stopped. Every import is deduplicated by txAdmin action id, so a repeat run adds only genuinely new bans and the console stays quiet unless something changed.

New config key: Config.TxImportLive (default auto) states whether the in-resource file is a symlink to live data or a static copy. A symlink is detected automatically and skips the staleness check; a copy keeps it, so an old snapshot can still never restore bans that were lifted after it was taken. Set it explicitly only if the detection guesses wrong.

fxadmin_txpath now ends with a VERDICT line naming the source that will actually be used and whether it counts as live or a copy. It also reports the byte count of the in-resource file, whether it parses as txAdmin data, and the date of the newest record it contains - enough to tell a working symlink from a stale copy at a glance.

Fixed: a double slash in the resource path (resources//[folder]/fx-admin, as some hosts report it) was carried into every candidate path fx-admin built and logged, breaking the directory walk that locates txData. The path is normalised before it is used.

The four places that each read txAdmin's ban file their own way - the startup check, the panel import, fxadmin_txrepair and the new timer - now share one reader, so they can no longer disagree about which source is available or whether it is live.

Fixed: the Discord page hung on its loading spinner forever once the bot had run its first command. A local variable in the usage-statistics block shadowed the panel's translation helper, so every label in that block threw instead of returning text, and the exception aborted the page render before any HTML reached the screen. The block is skipped while all counters are still zero, which is why the page opened normally on a fresh install and only broke after the first command - or the first denied attempt - was recorded.

Fixed: a ban lifted in txAdmin stayed banned in fx-admin when the revoke happened while the server was down. The live revoke event is only heard by a running server, and the periodic import skipped revoked actions instead of reconciling them, so the mirrored row survived every later sync and the player stayed banned by fx-admin alone. The import now deletes a mirrored ban whose txAdmin action has been revoked and tombstones the id so a later run cannot restore it. Matching is on the txAdmin action id and never on license - the bans table also holds bans fx-admin issued itself, and a license match would delete those too. The number cleaned up is reported as its own count in the import summary the admin sees, the console and the activity log.

Fixed: giving a vehicle to an online player reported "player not found". The call fails for two different reasons - the player's character data could not be read, or the spawn code is not in the vehicle catalogue - and it returns which one it was, but the panel threw that away and always showed the player error. An admin whose add-on car was simply missing from config_cars.lua was sent looking for a player who was standing right in front of them. The panel now reports the vehicle as not found when that is the real reason. The same call behind Discord's give-vehicle command compared the reason against a value the function never returns, so every failure there read as a player-data problem; it now names the spawn code it could not resolve and points at config_cars.lua.

New: an Activity tab on the Job and Gang Management pages. Pick a team and a window of 1, 3, 7, 14 or 30 days and it answers how many DIFFERENT members were online in it, how long each of them was on, how many separate days each showed up, and the day-by-day shape of the whole crew - enough to decide whether a gang has earned the business it is holding, and to see when one has gone quiet. Every playtime flush now also writes a per-day row carrying the job AND gang the character held at that moment, so someone who has since left still counts for the days they were a member and someone who joined yesterday does not retroactively inflate the crew - counting from today's roster gets both of those backwards. New table fx_admin_activity_daily, created automatically on start and also listed in setup/sql/fx_admin.sql; new config keys Config.Playtime.TeamActivity and Config.Playtime.ActivityKeepDays. There is nothing to backfill from: history starts the day this update is installed, so a 7 day window is only complete after 7 days.

Fixed: turning a Discord command's reason requirement off in the panel had no effect - admins kept being asked for a reason on /revive and others they had already switched off. The reason option is appended after a command's own arguments, and Discord refuses any command whose required options do not all come before the optional ones. /item, /weapon, /job, /gang and /teleport each carry an optional argument, so with a required reason all five produced a payload Discord rejects. A bot registers the whole command set in one call, so those five took the entire batch down with them and no setting from the panel ever reached Discord - including the ones on commands that were perfectly valid by themselves. Options are now ordered required-first before they are handed to the bot, so the payload stays valid whatever the reason is set to. Re-register the bot's slash commands once after updating; Discord keeps the old definitions until it is told otherwise.

Fixed: once the setup wizard had run, editing config.lua or config_server.lua did nothing for any setting the wizard manages - server name, framework, inventory, locale, theme, database tables, every webhook, the Discord bot token and guild, the bridge settings and the Discord panel owners. setup.json was applied over the config on every start, so the file plainly showed the value the owner wanted while the panel used another one, and nothing anywhere said so. The two are merged now instead of one overwriting the other: fx-admin remembers what the config file held when the two last agreed, so an edit to the file is recognised as an edit and wins, and the wizard's copy is updated to match. Change it in the panel and the panel wins, as before. Whichever side moved, both end up holding the same value. On the first start after this update neither side can be called newer, so the wizard still wins that round and every key where the two disagree is listed in the console instead of being dropped in silence - edit that line again and it takes over.

Fixed: a god could be missing a permission a moderator had. Permissions were read only from the group a player literally holds, with no inheritance between the tiers. The default config compensates by merging the three action lists by hand, but config.lua is customer-editable and kept across updates, so every action added in a later release is missing from an older config forever - which is how a server ends up with watchscreen listed for admin but not god, and a god-level admin who cannot open Monitor while a moderator can. god now inherits everything admin has and admin everything mod has, worked out at start from whatever the config lists. Inheritance can only add what a lower tier already holds, so it cannot hand out an action that was removed from every role, and a custom group still stands on its own list.

Fixed: Open Inventory silently did nothing. Every branch reported success whether or not the inventory resource had answered, and the caller discarded the result and wrote an Open Inventory line to the log regardless - so a failed open was indistinguishable from a working one from both the admin's side and the audit trail's. The real outcome is returned now and the admin is told which inventory failed and why: resource not running, export not answered, or the inventory script refusing that player. qs-inventory had no player-inventory branch at all and did nothing on every server running it; it is supported now. On qb-inventory and ps-inventory the fallback event was sent to the target player carrying their own id - it goes to the admin now, since it is the admin's screen that has to open, and the server export is tried first where the build has one.

New: items can be removed one at a time from the inventory viewer. Hover a slot and the delete button sits beside Detay. It appears only while the character is online, because removal runs through the live inventory script, and only for roles that may already wipe an inventory - it destroys items, so it sits behind the same permission rather than a weaker one. Works on tgiann-inventory, ox_inventory, qb-inventory, ps-inventory and qs-inventory, and both the success and the failure are logged with the item and amount.

Config.ServerOwner entries that could not be read were dropped in silence, which is the hardest possible way to find out an owner id has a typo: the file lists the person, the panel does not know them, and nothing explains why. Rejected lines are printed on start now, with the accepted formats and a pointer to the fxowner console command, which prints the real identifiers of everyone online ready to paste.

New: Cylex Phone is supported alongside lb-phone. The phone page reads whichever one's tables are actually in the database, decided at runtime rather than from a config key, so a server that switches phones only needs a restart. Number and account search, the Twitter, Instagram, Foffy (Cylex's short-video app, shown in the TikTok tab), Frogly marketplace and Yellow Pages feeds, post deletion and changing a character's number all work on both. Cylex keys everything on identifier and tag and holds the number once in cylex_phone_userdata, so each query joins back to it; likes and comments live in their own tables and are counted. Two fields have no Cylex equivalent and come back empty rather than invented: follower counts, and Frogly listings have no separate title, so the listing text fills it.

Fixed: the phone page printed the full failing SQL statement on every single lookup when the tables it reads do not exist - six errors per search, forever, on any server not running that phone script. A missing table is a permanent condition, so it is now reported once, by name, with a line saying which phone those tables belong to, and that query is skipped from then on.

Fixed: deleting or transferring a vehicle reported success even when the plate matched no row at all. Both ran their statement without waiting for it and returned true unconditionally, so a typo, an already-deleted vehicle or a plate stored with different padding produced a green 'vehicle deleted' toast and a clean line in the audit log while the database was untouched. Both now wait for the result and report 'vehicle not found' when nothing matched, and the log says FAILED with the plate.

Fixed: a Discord bot token set in config_server.lua was ignored once the setup wizard had run. The wizard writes an empty string for every optional field that was skipped, and that blank counted as a value and overwrote the config. A blank on one side now means 'not set here' rather than 'unset it everywhere', so whichever side holds the token is the one that is used - the same for the guild id and every webhook. Clearing a value therefore has to be done in the config file, not only in the wizard.

Fixed: giving or taking money from a character opened on the Characters page edited the database row instead of the live session. The drawer marks a row as OFFLINE whenever it was opened from a list that carries no server id - which is every row on that page, including characters whose owner is connected right then - and the money handler trusted that. The players row was updated while the running session kept its own copy: the panel showed the new balance, the HUD and the inventory kept showing the old one, and the framework wrote its in-memory value back over the edit at logout, quietly undoing it. The citizenid is now resolved against who is actually connected, so a live player always takes the live path. Changing a name or a phone number already worked this way.

Money and Give Item said nothing at all when the framework refused the change: the success branch was skipped and no other branch existed, so a failure looked like a success with a missing toast. Both report the failure now and write it to the audit log. Adding money through QBCore also returns its real result instead of an unconditional true.
